steps.title: Grow diatom cultures
steps.instruction: Inoculate 40 mL diatom cultures in 50 mL flasks and grow until mid‑ to end‑exponential phase; do not invert the flasks for at least 24 h before cryopreservation so cells settle at the bottom.

steps.title: Prepare DMSO media
steps.instruction: Make fresh culture medium (e.g., f/2) containing 24 % (v/v) DMSO; adjust DMSO amount if cultures are very dense so that the final DMSO concentration in the cryopreserved sample will be 12 %.

steps.title: Concentrate phytoplankton sample
steps.instruction: Remove the upper 30 mL of each culture flask without disturbing the diatom pellet at the bottom, leaving the concentrated biomass for cryopreservation.

steps.title: Cool isopropyl alcohol
steps.instruction: Place isopropyl alcohol (IPA) in a container and cool it to 4 °C.

steps.title: Mix sample with DMSO media
steps.instruction: Keep light intensity low, then combine the concentrated phytoplankton suspension with the DMSO‑containing medium in a 1:1 (50:50) ratio to achieve a final DMSO concentration of 12 %.

steps.title: Incubate and aliquot to cryovials
steps.instruction: Incubate the mixed suspension for 15–30 min under low light; during incubation transfer the suspension into cryovials, 1.6–1.8 mL per vial (volume depends on vial type), aiming for at least 6 replicates per original sample (18 replicates fit into one Mr Frosty). Keep the cryovials in the chilled Mr Frosty.

steps.title: Prepare Mr Frosty with cold IPA
steps.instruction: Fill the Mr Frosty container with the 4 °C IPA prepared earlier.

steps.title: Freeze samples in Mr Frosty
steps.instruction: Place the Mr Frosty (containing the cryovials) at –80 °C for at least 3–5 hours; do not close the Mr Frosty too tightly, otherwise the lid will be hard to open later.

steps.title: Transfer cryovials to LN2 storage
steps.instruction: After 3–6 hours remove the frozen cryovials, label each with a cryopreservation‑safe label, arrange them in a clearly ordered Cryobox, record the box location, and store the Cryobox in liquid nitrogen. Cryopreservation success can be assessed after at least 24 h in liquid nitrogen.

steps.title: Thaw cryovials in water bath
steps.instruction: Keep light low and place each cryovial in a 37 °C water bath until all ice crystals disappear (≈ 2 min).

steps.title: Dilute thawed sample in fresh media
steps.instruction: Under low light, add the thawed suspension to 45 mL of fresh culture medium to dilute the DMSO.

steps.title: Post‑thaw dark incubation
steps.instruction: Keep the diluted culture at 4 °C in the dark for 12 hours while maintaining low light conditions.

steps.title: Return to standard growth conditions
steps.instruction: After the 12‑hour dark period, raise the temperature to the standard growth temperature; after an additional 12 hours increase light intensity to the standard level.

steps.title: Monitor recovery
steps.instruction: Observe the cultures; recovery and growth may take several days to weeks.
